#DantePH Update (as of 5 p.m., 22 July 2025)
The low pressure area east of Aurora developed into tropical depression Dante.
Dante is not seen to make landfall but will enhance the southwest monsoon or habagat through Friday, July 25.
No wind signals are expected to be hoisted.
The enhanced habagat will bring significant rainfall over Luzon and some parts of Visayas.
Up to torrential rains may be expected over Pangasinan, Zambales, Bataan, Cavite, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro, and Metro Manila.
Serious threats of flooding and landslides remain.
Dante was spotted 1,130 km east of Northern Luzon at 4 p.m. Tuesday, with winds of 45 kph and gusts up to 55 kph. It is moving north northwestward at 20 kph.
The disturbance will intensify up to tropical storm strength while moving northwestward over the Philippine Sea.
It may exit the Philippine area of responsibility late Thursday or early Friday.
Meanwhile, the low pressure area near Batanes may either merge with the broader circulation of Dante or cross Extreme Northern Luzon towards the northern West Philippine Sea. #WeatherPatrol | via Ariel Rojas, ABS-CBN News

TROPICAL CYCLONE BULLETIN NR. 1
Tropical Depression #DantePH
Issued at 5:00 PM, 22 July 2025
Valid for broadcast until the next bulletin at 11:00 PM today.
THE LOW PRESSURE AREA EAST OF AURORA DEVELOPED INTO TROPICAL DEPRESSION “DANTE”
• Location of Center (4:00 PM):
The center of Tropical Depression DANTE was estimated based on all available data at 1,115 km East Northeast of Central Luzon or 1,130 km East of Northern Luzon (18.3°N, 132.4°E).
• Intensity:
Maximum su stained winds of 45 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 55 km/h, and central pressure of 1000 hPa
• Present Movement:
North northwestward at 20 km/h
• Extent of Tropical Cyclone Winds:
Strong winds extend outwards up to 220 km from the center
TROPICAL CYCLONE WIND SIGNALS (TCWS) IN EFFECT
• No Wind Signal currently hoisted.
OTHER HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND AREAS
• Heavy Rainfall Outlook
Refer to Weather Advisory No. 29 issued at 5:00 PM today for the heavy rainfall outlook due to the Southwest Monsoon enhanced by DANTE, the Low Pressure Area east of Batanes, and Tropical Cyclone WIPHA over Vietnam
• Severe Winds
The enhanced Southwest Monsoon will bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas (especially in coastal and upland areas exposed to winds):
• Today: Zambales, Bataan, Metro Manila, CALABARZON, MIMAROPA, Visayas, and Dinagat Islands
• Tomorrow (23 July): Ilocos Region, Zambales, Bataan, Bulacan, Metro Manila, CALABARZON, MIMAROPA, Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Camiguin, and Dinagat Islands.
• Friday (18 July): Ilocos Region, Abra, Benguet, Central Luzon, Metro Manila, CALABARZON, MIMAROPA, Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte Camiguin, and Dinagat Islands.
HAZARDS AFFECTING COASTAL WATERS
• 24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook
Up to rough seas over the following coastal waters:
• Up to 3.0 m: The seaboards of Batanes and Kalayaan Islands; the western seaboards of Zambales, Bataan, Lubang Island, Occidental Mindoro, and Calamian Islands.
• Mariners of small seacrafts, including all types of motorbancas, are advised not to venture out to sea under these conditions, especially if inexperienced or operating ill-equipped vessels.
Up to moderate seas over the following coastal waters:
• Up to 2.5 m: The seaboards of Babuyan Island and Ilocos Region; the southern seaboard of Bataan; the western seaboards of Cavite, Batangas, and Palawan.
• Up to 2.0 m: The seaboards of Camarines Norte, Oriental Mindoro, Marinduque, and Romblon; the northern and eastern seaboards of Catanduanes and Northern Samar; the eastern seaboards of Albay, Sorsogon and Davao Oriental; the western seaboard of Masbate; the southern seaboard of Quezon; the  remaining seaboard of Batangas and Occidental Mindoro; the northern seaboard of Camarines Sur.
• Mariners of motorbancas and similarly-sized vessels are advised to take precautionary measures while venturing out to sea and, if possible, avoid navigation under these conditions.
TRACK AND INTENSITY OUTLOOK
• DANTE is forecast to move northward or north northwestward over the Philippine Sea from tonight to tomorrow (23 July), before turning northwestward towards the Ryukyu Islands and the East China Sea. On the track forecast, DANTE may exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) on Thursday (24 July) or on Friday (25 July).
• DANTE may reach tropical storm category tomorrow. Further intensification into a severe tropical storm remains less likely but is not ruled out.
Considering these developments, the public and disaster risk reduction and management offices concerned are advised to take all necessary measures to protect life and property. Persons living in areas identified to be highly or very highly susceptible to these hazards are advised to follow evacuation and other instructions from local officials. For heavy rainfall warnings, thunderstorm/rainfall advisories, and other severe weather information specific to your area, please monitor products issued by your local PAGASA Regional Services Division.
The next tropical cyclone bulletin will be issued at 11:00 PM today.
DOST-PAGASA

The Department of Science and Technology (DOST) conducted the 8th National Research and Development Conference (NRDC) participated by government funding agencies, local government units, academe, and research and development institutes on July 23-24, 2025 at The Manila Hotel, City of Manila.
On the first day, DOST-PHIVOLCS and DOST-PAGASA facilitated the breakout session on Wealth Protection, one of the four pillars of DOST that intensifies the development and transfer of more climate and disaster-resilient technologies and provides science and technology-based information and services for warning, disaster preparedness, and mitigation.
Ms. Charmaine V. Villamil, DOST-PHIVOLCS Senior Science Research Specialist (SRS), provided the preliminaries and moderated the session. DOST-PHIVOLCS Director Teresito C. Bacolcol delivered the opening remarks and session overview.
Ms. Mabelline T. Cahulogan, Supervising SRS of DOST-PHIVOLCS, presented a topic on “Enhancing Disaster Resilience and Climate Adaptation: The Critical Role of Geospatial Technology in Safeguarding National Wealth in the Philippines.” Ms. Joan C. Salcedo, Supervising SRS of DOST-PHIVOLCS, imparted her insights on “Empowering Decision-Makers through REDAS: A Multi-Hazard Simulation and Impact Assessment Tool.” 
Other speakers were Secretary Robert E.A. Borje, Vice Chairperson and Executive Director of the Climate Change Commission; Mr. Emmanuel T. Balajadia of the Office of Civil Defense; and Dr. Marcelino Q. Villafuerte II, Deputy Administrator for Research and Development of DOST-PAGASA. Dr. Joseph Q. Basconcillo, Scientist I and Senior Weather Specialist of DOST-PAGASA, led the open forum and synthesis. The session ended with a closing remarks from Dr. Nathaniel T. Servando, DOST-PAGASA Administrator. 
In addition, DOST-PHIVOLCS showcased its DOST-funded "Accelerated Earthquake Multi-hazards Mapping and Risk Assessment Program of the Philippines" (ACER) Program in the exhibit hall.
With this year’s theme, “R&D Building Lives: Leveraging Transdisciplinary R&D for Well-being, Wealth Creation, Wealth Protection, and Sustainability,” the NRDC aims to promote multi-disciplinary and collaborative R&D, to coordinate and rationalize the R&D agenda, to harmonize all R&D agenda and priorities, and to facilitate dissemination of outputs of programs and projects under the Harmonized National R&D Agenda to various research institutions and agencies.

Maximum sustained winds of 75 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 90 km/h, and central pressure of 994 hPa.

Northward at 15 km/h

Strong to gale-force winds extend outwards up to 550 km from the center

Forecast wave heights are not related to storm surge heights.

ATM: REDAS Training Reaches Sorsogon Province
DOST-PHIVOLCS leads a training on "Mainstreaming Disaster Risk Reduction into the Local Development, Contingency, and Emergency Preparedness Planning Process through the Use of REDAS Software" for Sorsogon Province. 
The training, held at Cristina’s Resort and Hotel, Sorsogon City on July 21-25, 2025, features three modules including REDAS function to simulate earthquake hazards, such as ground shaking, liquefaction, landslides, and tsunami.

Maica Mendoza took advantage of the floods on Friday, July 25, by showcasing her waders live through an online shopping platform, believing that seeing how her items work in the real-life scenario would boost her sales.
Mendoza’s unique live-selling strategy, which she said started back in 2020, has garnered a steady following of over 32,000 followers on TikTok. She lives in Calumpit, Bulacan, which is prone to floods during typhoon or monsoon seasons.
Typhoon #EmongPH made landfall in the province of Pangasinan early morning Friday and has since weakened to a tropical storm after crossing the mountainous region and exiting the landmass of Luzon.

What options does the Senate have in asserting to convene as an impeachment court, when the decision of the Supreme Court says it is immediately executory? University of the Philippines constitutional law professor John Molo weighs in.
https://www.rappler.com/.../analysis-supreme-court-sara.../ WATCH:What happens if Senate proceeds to try VP Sara Duterte despite SC order? What options does the Senate have in asserting to convene as an impeachment court, when the decision of the Supreme Court says it is immediately executory? University of the Philippines constitutional law professor John Molo weighs in. https://www.rappler.com/.../analysis-supreme-court-sara.../ The Judiciary is a human institution, and it has erred so many times before. There have been moments were it shirked from its solemn role to uphold and defend the Constitution. Among others: In Javellana v. Executive Secretary (G.R. No. L-36142, March 31, 1973) for example, the Supreme Court virtually dodged its obligation to check whether the ratification of the 1973 Constitution by the Marcos Administration was done properly when it hid behind technicalities through the motness and political question doctrines. Justice Tehankee’s dissent stated that “ours is a government of laws, not of men. And when the highest Court of the land looks the other way while the fundamental law is being torn asunder, it ceases to be a court of justice.” In de Leon v. Duterte, (G.R. No. 253118, May 8, 2020) the Supreme Court dismissed a Petition for Mandamus for the disclosure of the President’s health records during the height of the pandemic without even requiring a comment from the Solicitor General. In his dissent, Justice Leonen said that “The Court missed an opportunity to affirm that in a constitutional democracy, even the most powerful are answerable to the people.” In Republic v. Sereno (G.R. No. 237428, May 12, 2018), the Supreme Court shattered the most basic rule that impeachable officials may only be removed by impeachment. The dissenters therein said that “The majority has obliterated the carefully crafted system of checks and balances embedded in our Constitution” and “We have become enablers of impunity. Today, we weaken the very institution we are sworn to protect.” Given the above, let’s not even have the illusion that the Supreme Court is always right. In the book of Marites Danguilan Vitug, she reminded all of us that “the Court is not as cloistered or as independent as many believe. It breathes the same air as the political branches of government.” Today is indeed a sad day for checks and balances in this country. While the decision is not yet out for public consumption, it has already created the impression that the Supreme Court has decided to arrogate upon itself a power that was exclusively supposed to be vested in the House of Representatives and it has failed to stay in its own lane. Worse, some comments I see already perceive the institution as a protector of the Dutertes as the majority of the justices were appointed by Rodrigo Duterte. There is still an opportunity for the Supreme Court to correct what I respectfully submit is a huge mistake it has committed. Hopefully, it will reverse itself after the proper filing of a motion for reconsideration. Otherwise, trust in the Judiciary as an institution may further be eroded and it will become an institution that may be considered as so damaged that I am uncertain if it will ever be the same again. - Atty. Dino Singson De leon

House to appeal SC’s ruling on impeachment case vs Sara Duterte House to appeal SC’s ruling on impeachment case vs Sara Duterte The Judiciary is a human institution, and it has erred so many times before. There have been moments were it shirked from its solemn role to uphold and defend the Constitution. Among others: In Javellana v. Executive Secretary (G.R. No. L-36142, March 31, 1973) for example, the Supreme Court virtually dodged its obligation to check whether the ratification of the 1973 Constitution by the Marcos Administration was done properly when it hid behind technicalities through the motness and political question doctrines. Justice Tehankee’s dissent stated that “ours is a government of laws, not of men. And when the highest Court of the land looks the other way while the fundamental law is being torn asunder, it ceases to be a court of justice.” In de Leon v. Duterte, (G.R. No. 253118, May 8, 2020) the Supreme Court dismissed a Petition for Mandamus for the disclosure of the President’s health records during the height of the pandemic without even requiring a comment from the Solicitor General. In his dissent, Justice Leonen said that “The Court missed an opportunity to affirm that in a constitutional democracy, even the most powerful are answerable to the people.” In Republic v. Sereno (G.R. No. 237428, May 12, 2018), the Supreme Court shattered the most basic rule that impeachable officials may only be removed by impeachment. The dissenters therein said that “The majority has obliterated the carefully crafted system of checks and balances embedded in our Constitution” and “We have become enablers of impunity. Today, we weaken the very institution we are sworn to protect.” Given the above, let’s not even have the illusion that the Supreme Court is always right. In the book of Marites Danguilan Vitug, she reminded all of us that “the Court is not as cloistered or as independent as many believe. It breathes the same air as the political branches of government.” Today is indeed a sad day for checks and balances in this country. While the decision is not yet out for public consumption, it has already created the impression that the Supreme Court has decided to arrogate upon itself a power that was exclusively supposed to be vested in the House of Representatives and it has failed to stay in its own lane. Worse, some comments I see already perceive the institution as a protector of the Dutertes as the majority of the justices were appointed by Rodrigo Duterte. There is still an opportunity for the Supreme Court to correct what I respectfully submit is a huge mistake it has committed. Hopefully, it will reverse itself after the proper filing of a motion for reconsideration. Otherwise, trust in the Judiciary as an institution may further be eroded and it will become an institution that may be considered as so damaged that I am uncertain if it will ever be the same again. - Atty. Dino Singson De leon

But for Agustin, who is eternally grateful for the rare opportunity to live out his dream, he thanks his fans for their patience and support, and most importantly, God, for being by his side.

𝐅𝐨𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: The key difference between a 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 and a 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐲 lies in their forecast period, coverage areas, and accuracy. A 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 provides forecasts for the next three hours and applies up to the municipal level. The Office of Civil Defense (OCD) warns the public against the circulation of deceptive text messages that falsely claim individuals may receive financial aid or other forms of government assistance. These fraudulent messages often misuse the name or official SMS number of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) and contain suspicious links. The public is strongly advised not to click on any such links, even if the message appears to come from an official source.
The NDRRMC SMS number is strictly used for disseminating disaster alerts and early warnings. It is not intended for the distribution of aid, cash transfers, or any personal transactions.
Scammers often exploit heightened emotions and urgency during disasters by launching fake donation drives, phishing schemes, and fraudulent messages aimed at stealing personal information or financial resources. In some cases, they impersonate typhoon victims, volunteers, or government personnel, using fabricated stories and stolen images to solicit donations or sensitive data.
The OCD strongly condemns the actions of individuals or groups who exploit disasters and the suffering of affected communities for fraudulent or malicious purposes and urges everyone to exercise vigilance and caution. Verify before clicking on links or sharing any information. Only trust official government websites and verified platforms. Report suspicious messages to your telecommunications provider or the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) via the One Stop Public Assistance Center (OSPAC) at (02) 8924-4010 or by email at consumer@ntc.gov.ph. You may also contact the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) via their Inter-Agency Response Center (IARC) at 1326 or report online through report@cicc.gov.ph.
For those seeking government assistance, please refer only to the official channels of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) or other authorized agencies. Official updates, advisories, and announcements are published exclusively on their verified websites and social media pages.
In times of crisis, generosity and compassion are essential—but they must be paired with responsibility and discernment. By remaining alert and verifying information, we not only protect ourselves but also ensure that help reaches those who truly need it.

The DOST-PHIVOLCS, in collaboration with DOST XII, Office of Civil Defense (OCD) XII, Philippine Information Agency (PIA) XII, and Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) XII, held its “PHIVOLCS InfoPress: Understanding and Communicating Geologic Hazards Information in Region XII” on July 29, 2025 at Greenleaf Hotel, General Santos City.
Mr. Abdul Jalil D. Malawan, Supervising Science Research Specialist (SRS) of DOST XII, welcomed the participants, composed of media practitioners, government information officers, and Disaster Risk Reduction frontliners across Central Mindanao.
Resource speakers from DOST-PHIVOLCS provided comprehensive discussions on volcano, earthquake, and tsunami information.
Mr. Jeffrey S. Perez, Supervising SRS, led a session on “Beneath the Surface: Understanding the Big One in Region XII.” Ms. Joan C. Salcedo, Supervising SRS, discussed a topic on “From Crest to Trough: Understanding the Science of Tsunami.”
Further, Ms. Charmaine V. Villamil, Senior SRS, shared an insight on “Land and Lava: Living with Active Volcanoes.” She also moderated the open forum to give the participants an opportunity to ask questions related to the topics.
In the afternoon, Mr. Christian R. Matullano, Information Officer II of PIA XII, talked about “#MagingMapanuri Campaign: Dismissing Disinformation.” Ms. Melissa Mae T. Garcia, SRS of DOST-PHIVOLCS, facilitated the “GeoTalks: Review of Commonly-used Geologic Terms”. Afterward, participants took part in a return demonstration workshop. Mr. Raylindo S. Aniñon, Regional Director of OCD XII, delivered his closing remarks.
Having experienced many earthquakes in the region for the past months, this event shares the mission in equipping our partners from the media in communicating the right information on geologic hazards and their impact on the community.

KANLAON VOLCANO BULLETIN
29 July 2025
6:30 PM
This serves as a notice for the lowering of Kanlaon Volcano’s status from Alert Level 3 (magmatic unrest / high level of volcanic unrest) to Alert Level 2 (moderate level of volcanic unrest).
Following its last eruptive activity on 13 May 2025, Kanlaon Volcano has been exhibiting less frequent volcanic earthquake activity, decreased volcanic gas emitted by subsurface magma and ground deformation cycles. These observations are supported by the following monitoring parameters:
1. Volcanic earthquakes recorded by the Kanlaon Volcano Network (KVN) averaged 8 events/day with peak magnitudes of ML2.7 for the period 14 May 2025 to present (Figure 1A). This marks a significant decrease from the medium-term average of 14 events/day with peak magnitudes of ML3.8 for the period 3 June 2024 to 13 May 2025. Volcano-tectonic or VT earthquakes generated by rock fracturing within the edifice continue to dominate earthquake activity at Kanlaon. These have mostly originated along a northwest to southeast transect of the edifice at depths of 0 to 15 kilometers below mean sea level (Figure 2), suggesting a structurally controlled deep magmatic intrusion that is driving unrest. Despite the decline in volcanic earthquake events, however, overall seismic energy release by the volcano, as shown by real-time seismic amplitude or RSAM records (Figure 1C), has not significantly decreased, highlighting uncertainty in the volcano’s declining seismic behavior. 
2. Ash emission from the summit crater (Figure 1B), which began in October 2024, has ceased after the last event on 5 June 2025. Since then, activity at the crater has transitioned to quiet degassing of steam-dominated plumes. A total of 306 ash emission events have been recorded since 19 October 2024, while a total of five explosive eruptions have occurred between 3 June 2024 and 13 May 2025.
3. Sulfur dioxide or SO2 flux based on campaign spectrometry (Figure 1D) has likewise declined to an average of 1,857 tonnes/day for the period 13 May 2025 to present. Average SO2 flux in excess of 4,400 tonnes/day persisted between the 3 June 2024 and 6 February 2025 explosive eruptions but began to decrease in March 2025. Decreased degassing at Kanlaon could indicate a pause in the intrusion of, or depletion of volcanic gas in, magma within the shallower levels of the edifice, or the sealing of magmatic gas pathways. 
4. Ground swelling or inflation of the Kanlaon edifice has been unsteadily sustained at low rates since 2022 based on continuous Global Positioning System (GPS) monitoring and indicated in the short-term as well by Electronic Distance Measurements since 2024 (Figure 3). A short-term deflation of the edifice began in the last week of June to first week of July 2025, suggesting a pause in the intrusion of magma or depressurization due to the reduction of volcanic gas in the volcanic system, consistent with SO2 flux data.
In view of the above observations, DOST-PHIVOLCS is lowering the alert status of Kanlaon Volcano from Alert Level 3 to Alert Level 2 to reflect the overall decreasing trend in the level of monitoring parameters. Alert Level 2 means that there is decreased unrest but should not be interpreted that unrest has ceased or that the threat of an eruption has disappeared, given that magma has already been intruded deep beneath the edifice. Should an uptrend or pronounced change in monitored parameters forewarn of potential eruption, the Alert Level may be raised back to Alert Level 3. At such time, people residing within areas at high risk to pyroclastic density currents or PDCs who have returned after the step-down to Alert Level 2 must therefore be prepared for a quick and organized evacuation.  Conversely, should there be a persistent downtrend in monitored parameters after a sufficient observation period, the Alert Level will be further lowered to Alert Level 1. 
DOST-PHIVOLCS strongly recommends that at Alert Level 2, communities within the 4-km radius Permanent Danger Zone or PDZ should remain evacuated due to the lingering chances of short-lived explosive eruptions and sudden steam-driven or phreatic explosions that can generate life-threatening volcanic hazards such as PDCs, ballistic projectiles, rockfalls and lethal expulsions of volcanic gas. Local government units must continue to prepare their communities within the PDC hazard zone for subsequent evacuation in case unrest re-escalates and progresses into magmatic eruption. Increased vigilance against potential lahars and sediment-laden streamflows in channels draining the volcanic slopes must continually be exercised in case eruptive unrest resumes under heavy to intense rainfall. Civil aviation authorities must also advise pilots to avoid flying close to the volcano’s summit as ash from any sudden eruption can be hazardous to aircraft.

As part of ongoing Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Response (HADR) efforts in Northern Luzon, the United States Air Force (USAF) deployed its CV-22 Osprey aircraft to support the Philippine Air Force's (PAF) air assets in airlifting relief supplies to typhoon-affected communities in Basco, Batanes.
A total of 300 boxes of family food packs were airlifted aboard the USAF CV-22 Osprey, from Clark Air Base, Pampanga to Basco, Batanes. PAF personnel from the Tactical Operations Wing Northern Luzon (TOWNOL), provided essential ground support during the joint PH-US mission, assisting in the unloading, handling, and coordination of aid distribution in Basco, Batanes.
A day earlier, on July 29, 2025, the PAF deployed its C-130 and Black Hawk aircraft to transport batches of relief goods to Batanes and Abra, respectively. The C-130 aircraft also facilitated the transport of locally stranded individuals (LSIs) from Basco to Manila on its return flight.

Inaasahan na hanggang 17 na bagyo ang maaaring mabuo o pumasok ng Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) simula buwan ng Agosto 2025 hanggang Enero 2026.
Makikita sa infographic na nasa ibaba ang climatological tracks ng mga bagyong dumaan at pumasok ng PAR mula taong 1948 hanggang 2015 at ang bilang ng mga bagyo na maaring mabuo kada buwan.

PANOORIN: Buwis-buhay na pagtawid sa ilog ang kailangang suungin ng mga residente sa  Brgy. Tinucan, Tanay, Rizal para lamang makarating sa bayan upang makapamili ng mga pagkain.
Kuwento ni YouScooper Rona Nikka Biason tungkol sa unang video rito na kinuha nitong July 23, isang lalaki ang hindi nag-alinlangan na magkabit ng lubid sa puno sa kabila ng ilog upang magkaroon ng balsa bilang pansamantalang transportasyon ng mga residente doon. 
"Sana mabigyang pansin ng ating gobyerno ang halos dekada na naming hinaing na sana kahit tulay na pantao lang ay malagyan ito," ayon kay Rona na kumuha ng video. 
Nakararanas umano sila ng biglang pagtaas ng tubig sa ilog dahilan upang umabot ng lampas-leeg hanggang lampas-tao ang taas nito. Makikita rito ang ilan pang video na pinadala ni YouScooper Rona na nangyari umano sa mga sumunod na araw, mula July 24 hanggang 26, 2025.
Dagdag ni Rona noong mga araw na iyon, mayroong tulay na maaaring daanan pero kailangan pa ring tumawid sa ilog, at mayroon ding ibang daanan pero may mga nakaharang na landslide.
Matapos magpadala ang GMA Integrated News noong July 25 ng paglagom ng hinaing ni YouScooper Rona at link patungo sa kaniyang video sa Facebook, sinabi ng Tanay LGU na inendorso na ang hinaing.
"Magalang po naming ipinababatid na amin pong naendorso ang naturang liham sa kinauukulang opisina para sa kinakailangang aksyon sa inyong hinaing," sinabi ni Dr. Jeffrey Pino, municipal administrator ng Tanay, Rizal, nitong July 31 sa pamamagitan ng email. #Youscoop

The DOST-PAGASA in partnership with the GCF Multi-hazard Impact-based Forecasting and Early Warning System for the Philippines (MHIFEWS) Project conducted a 2025 Rainfall Warning System (RWS) Conference this August 1, 2025, at the Madison 101 Hotel with the goal of improving and harmonizing rainfall warning system issued nationwide.
Attended by PAGASA key officials and representatives from R&D, Operations, and Engineering and Technical Services Divisions, current best practices that can be adopted, as well as existing challenges and gaps that need to be addressed were tackled in the conference.
Mark Ivan C. Roblas, Supervising Science Research Specialist of DOST-PCIEERD Information Group, served as a resource speaker and shared his expertise in science communication. In his presentation, he emphasized the importance of effectively communicating with audiences and stakeholders. He also provided suggestions on how to further improve PAGASA’s current Rainfall Warning System (RWS) through enhanced messaging strategies, audience engagement, and alignment with impact-based forecasting practices.
A moderated discussion was conducted to gather inputs from forecasters  on ways to improve RWS operational procedures, and strategies to align with PAGASA's Multi-Hazard Impact-Based Early Warning System initiative.
After the session, a technical working group composed of representatives from various PRSDs and relevant divisions will be reconstituted to update the Manual of Operations and Standard Operating Procedures, addressing the current and future needs of the Agency’s stakeholders as highlighted during the conference.

WHERE IS THE PRESIDENT NOW?
While Typhoon Crising lashes the Philippines, leaving entire towns flooded, homes destroyed, and Filipinos crying for help, our President is abroad—comfortably meeting with the US President.
 This is leadership?
In the face of calamity, when his people need him the most, he chooses to leave. No direct presence, no leadership on the ground. Just silence. Is this the kind of leader we deserve?
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, the President is the Commander-in-Chief and must be present and accountable in times of national emergency. Leaving the country without declaring who is in command violates his constitutional duties.
 LEGAL BASIS: 
 Article VII, Section 4 – The President shall ensure the faithful execution of the laws and must uphold accountability to the people.
 Article XI, Section 1 – Public officers, including the President, must at all times be accountable to the people.
 Article XI, Section 2 – The President may be removed from office on impeachment for culpable violation of the Constitution, betrayal of public trust, or gross neglect of duty.
 Abandoning the nation during a declared State of Calamity without properly delegating emergency authority can be considered gross negligence and betrayal of public trust.
Is this the kind of leader we want — one who leaves during disaster? Or do we deserve someone who will stand and lead in the storm?
 Is this the kind of leader we deserve?

Nais ituwid ng Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) ang lumabas na news article ng ABS-CBN kung saan nakasaad na hindi exempted ang mga emergency vehicle sa No Contact Apprehension Policy (NCAP).
Sa panayam kay MMDA Chairman Atty. Don Artes ng isang ABS-CBN reporter, malinaw niyang sinabi na hindi awtomatikong exempted sa mga traffic violations ang mga emergency vehicle. Hindi lahat ng may blinkers at sirena ay exempted sa batas-trapiko. Isa ito sa dahilan kung bakit hindi pwede automatic ang exemption. 
Kinakailangang masiguro na lehitimong emergency vehicle ang sasakyan. Hindi dapat iprograma sa NCAP system na lahat ng may blinkers at siren ay automatic na exempt sa huli dahil maaring may manamantala nito. 
Nagkaroon na ng insidente kung saan ang isang funeral vehicle ay nagpanggap na "ambulance" para makadaan sa EDSA Busway. Nahuli ito ng Special Action and Intelligence Committee for Transportation (SAICT).
Sa ilalim ng NCAP, ang mga mahuhuli ng AI-technology CCTV cameras ay sasailalim sa automatic review. Ibig sabihin, mano-mano itong rerebyuhin ng aming NCAP personnel. Kapag napatunayang mali ang pagkakahuli, i-invalidate ito at hindi makatatanggap ng notice of violation.
Kung walang emergency, hindi dapat lumalabag sa mga traffic rules ang mga emergency vehicle.
Umaasa ang MMDA na sa tulong ng mga media entities, maihahatid ang impormasyon sa publiko nang tama at beripikado.
